newsitem.title: UK: DMG sees no pension fund exodus.
newsitem.headline: DMG sees no pension fund exodus.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the investment banking arm of Deutsche Bank, said on Thursday it does not expect any exodus of its pension fund clients following the suspension of UK pension fund division head, Nicola Horlick.
"The first thing we did after the suspension was announced was to tell our clients," said DMG spokesman James Murray. "The feedback was that they are not going to make any hasty decisions."
Horlick, head of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management's 18 billion stg UK pension find operation and an industry high-flyer, was suspended on Tuesday for "possible breach of contract".

Murray said DMG's clients understand that their business is managed by a team and not just an individual and will take their decisions based on performance which, he added, had been "consistently high over a one, three and five year timescale."

Some pension funds have complained that DMG should be saying more about why Horlick was suspended to end uncertainty, even though DMG has made clear that there is no question of financial impropriety.
But the bank insists it has to follow procedures closely in what is an internal matter and that it would be unfair to Horlick to say any more at this point.
There has been intense press speculation that Horlick was preparing a move to Dutch bank ABN AMRO, possibly with several of her colleagues, but ABN has denied trying to poach DMG staff.
